cases.description: When the JSON node contains a `$schema` tag with a known Draft‑07 URI, `detect` should return the corresponding `VersionFlag.DRAFT_07`.
When the JSON node contains a `$schema` tag with a known Draft‑04 URI, `detect` should return the corresponding `VersionFlag.DRAFT_04`.
When the JSON node contains a `$schema` tag with a known 2020‑12 URI, `detect` should return the corresponding `VersionFlag.DRAFT_2020_12`.
If the JSON node does not contain a `$schema` field, `detect` must throw a `JsonSchemaException` with the message `'$schema' tag is not present`.
If the `$schema` field is present but its value is not recognised by `detectOptionalVersion`, the optional result is empty and `detect` should throw a `JsonSchemaException` with the same message.
Calling `detect` with a null JsonNode should raise a NullPointerException because the method attempts to access the node without a null‑check.

When the `$schema` field exists but its value is not a text node (e.g., a number), `detectOptionalVersion` cannot map it to a known version, so `detect` should throw a `JsonSchemaException` with the standard message.
If `$schema` is an array (or any non‑string JSON type), the detector treats it as unknown and throws the same `JsonSchemaException`.
The detector recognises the Draft‑06 URI and returns `VersionFlag.DRAFT_06`.
The detector recognises the Draft‑2019‑09 URI (newer URL style) and returns `VersionFlag.DRAFT_2019_09`.
The detector also recognises the legacy Draft‑2019‑09 URI with a trailing `#`.
Leading/trailing whitespace is not trimmed by the detector; the exact string does not match any known URI, resulting in an exception.
The detector performs a case‑sensitive match; an upper‑cased URI is considered unknown and triggers the exception.
An empty string value for `$schema` cannot be mapped to any version, so `detect` throws the standard `JsonSchemaException`.

group: detect - $schema with fragment or query parameters

cases.description: Appending a fragment or extra characters to a known URI makes it unrecognised; the detector should throw the exception.
A known URI with a query string is not matched by the detector, leading to an exception.

group: detect - root node not an object

cases.description: When the root JSON node is an empty array, the detector cannot find a `$schema` field and throws the standard `JsonSchemaException`.
When the root JSON node is a numeric literal, the detector treats it as missing `$schema` and throws the standard `JsonSchemaException`.
When the root JSON node is a boolean literal, the detector cannot locate a `$schema` field and throws the standard `JsonSchemaException`.
When the root JSON node is a plain string (not an object), the detector does not find a `$schema` field and throws the standard `JsonSchemaException`.
When the `$schema` field is present but its value is JSON null, the detector cannot map it to a known version and throws the standard `JsonSchemaException`.
